ex-checkout.name: One-page checkout
ex-checkout.goal: Cut checkout from six steps to one so more carts become orders.
ex-checkout.objectiveText: Make paying for an order effortless on mobile
ex-checkout.decisionNote: Needs the mobile abandonment baseline and one more usability round before the review.

history.note: Small lift from the saved-card fix

text.problem: Checkout has six screens. 42% of people who start checkout leave before paying, and on mobile it's worse.
text.customer: Returning shoppers on mobile, 61% of checkout starts.
text.alternatives: Competitors moved to single-page checkout. Today's workaround is calling support to place the order.
text.whynow: The payments migration in Q1 already touches every checkout screen, so we rebuild once.
text.whyus: We already store addresses and payment methods for 80% of returning customers.
text.factors: Payments migration lands on time. Tax service supports a single quote call.
text.solution: One screen with address, delivery and payment stacked, pre-filled for returning customers.
text.value: Prototype test: 6 of 6 participants preferred it to today's flow.
text.feasibility: Spike done: front end 6 weeks, tax quote change 2 weeks.
text.tldr: Mobile checkout loses 42% of shoppers across six screens. We'll replace it with one pre-filled screen, piloting express pay first. Success is cart-to-order conversion from 58% to 66% by year end.
text.background: Checkout was last redesigned in 2021 for desktop. Mobile is now 61% of checkout starts, and the payments migration in Q1 touches every screen anyway.
text.goals:
Goals: fewer steps, faster payment, the same fraud rate.
Non-goals: new payment providers, changes to the cart, desktop layout.
text.nfr: Checkout screen loads in under 1.5 s on 4G at p75. WCAG 2.2 AA. Copy in English, French (Quebec) and Spanish (US).
text.scope:
In: one-page checkout for returning customers on mobile, express pay pilot.
Later: guest checkout on one page.
Out: desktop redesign.
text.launch: Express pay pilot in two cities behind a flag, then 10%, 50%, 100% of mobile over four weeks. Roll back by turning the flag off.
text.legal: Terms acceptance placement needs legal sign-off. Card data stays with the payment provider.

text.size: If half of today's drop-offs activate, that is about 1,200 more active accounts a year.
